sentences.text: Shri Sushil Goswami, learned counsel for appellants.

Dr. Anjali Gyanani, learned Public Prosecutor for respo Per Justice Milind Ramesh Phadke Heard on I.A.No. 2947 of 2024, third repeat application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant No.2 - Sunil and I.A. No.10637 of 2024, first application under Section 389 (1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant No.1- Sushil Singh.

Both the appellants stand convicted under Section 302/34 and 304B of I.P.C and are sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with a fine of Rs.2000/-, further they are convicted under Section 498A of I.P.C and are sentenced to undergo two years' R.I. with a fine of Rs.1000/-, and under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and are sentenced to undergo one year R.I. with a fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulations respectively vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 28.02.2019 passed by Third Additional Sessions Judge Bhind (M.P.) in S.T. No.284/2013.
Appellant No.1-Sushil so far has undergone jail sentence of about eight years and five months and appellant No.2-Sunil so far has undergone jail sentence of about five years and five months.
The case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 11.06.2012, marriage was solemnized between appellant No.1 Sushil Singh and deceased Pooja.

On 28.04.2013 at about 4:30 to 5 pm, her family members took deceased Pooja, 2 CRA-3021-2019 who got burnt due to fire, to Mihona Hospital,
thereafter Bhind and Gwalior.
Chowkidar Dayal Singh gave information that deceased Pooja - daughter-in-law of Thakur Than Singh got burnt by kerosene oil.

On the said information, Station House Officer, Police Station-Mihona initiated the proceedings and dying declaration of the deceased Pooja Ex.P-5 was recorded in which though initially she did not involve anyone, but in the dying declaration Ex.P-12 recorded on the second day, she disclosed that her husband Sushil Singh poured kerosene oil on her, her Jeth Sunil gave matchstick to her husband and her husband set her ablaze.
She further disclosed that the accused persons used to harass her.
After investigation, the FIR was registered and the investigation was set in motion.
Unfortunately, she succumbed to the burn injuries sustained by her while undergoing treatment.
Upon completion of the investigation including recording of statements, collection of evidence and necessary formalities, challan was filed.
The Sessions Court, on appreciation of evidence placed on record, convicted and sentenced the present appellants, as mentioned above.

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for appellants while taking exception to the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence submits that the Sessions Court has not appreciated the evidence placed on record in correct perspective.
The judgment suffers from surmises and conjectures.
It is submitted that the present appellants have falsely been implicated in the instant case.
It is further submitted that there are two dying declarations in the matter.

First dying declaration was recorded on 28.04.2013 by Executive Magistrate, Tehsil Bhind, in which the deceased did not implicate any of the accused persons whereas in the another dying declaration which was recorded on 29.04.2013 by Naib Tehsildar, the deceased alleged that her Jeth gave matchstick to her husband and her husband 3 CRA-3021-2019 set her ablaze.
Hence, there are a lot of inconsistencies and discrepancies in both the dying declarations.

It is further submitted that appellant No.1-Sushil so far has undergone jail sentence of about eight years and five months and appellant No.2-Sunil so far has undergone jail sentence of about five years and five months as he was on bail during trial.

On these grounds,
learned counsel submits that the appellant No.1 and 2 may be extended the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor, appearing on behalf of the respondent/State, while supporting the judgment impugned submits that no exception can be taken in the matter of suspension of sentence and grant of bail, regard being had to the nature and the gravity of offence found proved against the present appellants.

Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, though this Court refrains from commenting upon the rival contentions advanced touching the merits of the case, but regard being had to the fact that there are a lot of inconsistencies and discrepancies in both the dying declarations and appellant No.1-Sushil so far has undergone jail sentence of about eight years and five months and appellant No.2-Sunil so far has undergone jail sentence of about five years and five months.

and the appeal being of the year 2019 is not likely to be decided in near further, we are of the view that appellant No.1 - Sushil and appellant No.2- Sunil are entitled to the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Accordingly,I.A.No. 2947 of 2024 and I.A. No.10637 of 2024 stand allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of appellant No.1- Sushil Singh and appellant No.2 - Sunil shall remain suspended during pendency of the present appeal and they shall be released on bail subject to verification of the 4 CRA-3021-2019 factum of depositing the fine amount and on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lac Only) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
Appellant No.1- Sushil Singh and appellant No.2 - Sunil are directed to appear before the Registry of this Court first on 14.10.2024 and on other subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf.
Accordingly, the said IAs stand allowed and disposed of.
Observations on facts, if any, are only for the purpose of deciding the instant I.As. and shall have no bearing on the merits of the appeal.
